title: Why are sunsets red and orange?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why is the sky red at sunset?
Why does the Sun look orange when it sets?
Why are some sunsets more colourful?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: A longer path through air leaves the reds

explain.say: Sunsets turn the sky red, orange and pink. The same scattering that makes the sky blue also makes sunsets red; what changes is how much air the light has to cross.

draw.text: Why are sunsets red and orange?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: A longer path through air leaves the reds

explain.say: At midday the Sun is high, and its light takes a short path through the air to reach you. Only some blue is scattered out, so the Sun looks white-yellow and the sky around it is blue.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: A longer path through air leaves the reds

explain.say: At sunset the Sun is low, so its light skims through many times more air before it reaches you. Along the way almost all the blue and green is scattered aside, leaving mostly red and orange.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: A longer path through air leaves the reds

explain.say: Dust, smoke, sea salt and other tiny particles add to the effect, which is why sunsets after volcanic eruptions or wildfires can be especially fiery. Meanwhile the scattered blue light is lighting someone else's daytime sky.

faq.q: Why is the Sun red when it sets?
faq.a: Its light travels through much more air when it is low on the horizon. Most of the blue is scattered out along the way, so mostly red and orange light reaches your eyes.
asks: Why does the sunset look orange?
Why is the sky red in the evening?

faq.q: How much more air does sunset light pass through?
faq.a: When the Sun is right on the horizon, its light crosses roughly 38 times as much air as when it is straight overhead. That long path strips out the blue.
asks: Why does a low Sun look different?

faq.q: Why are some sunsets more colourful than others?
faq.a: Dust, smoke, sea salt and other tiny particles in the air add more scattering. After a big volcanic eruption or wildfire, sunsets can be extra red for weeks or months.
asks: Why are sunsets redder after a volcano?

faq.q: Is sunrise red for the same reason?
faq.a: Yes. At sunrise the Sun is also low, so its light takes the same long path through the air and loses its blue.

faq.q: Does red sky at night mean good weather?
faq.a: Sometimes. Where weather moves from west to east, a red sunset means clear, dry air to the west, which is often heading your way. It is a rule of thumb, not a forecast.
asks: Is red sky at night shepherd's delight true?

facts: When the Sun is on the horizon its light passes through roughly 38 times as much air as when it is overhead.
After the 1883 eruption of Krakatoa, sunsets around the world were unusually red for months.
